newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba launches computers with Intel MMX.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba launches computers with Intel MMX.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said on Thursday that it had started selling notebook and desktop computers which use Intel Corp's MMX technology Pentium processors.

The MMX Pentium chip, which was unveiled on Wednesday, is a new multimedia chip which analysts say will quickly become the new standard for the industry, allowing Intel to maintain its dominance over the semiconductor market.
The chip supports various multimedia functions, including video and audio data processing.

Toshiba started selling its BREZZA 5200VMB home-use desktop personal computer (PC) in Japan on Thursday at 568,000 yen. The PC, which uses MMX processors, incorporates a digital video disc (DVD) drive.

Toshiba also launched a TECRA 740 notebook PC model on the global market on Thursday, again using MMX processors. The PC has a 13.3-inch thin-film-transistor colour liquid crystal display which can display 16.77 million colours simultaneously.
The notebook is priced at 828,000 yen.
The firm said it would introduce another notebook model worldwide on February 3, the TECRA 730X, which also uses MMX processors, Toshiba said.
It said the model would be priced at 748,000 yen.
